topic: Implicit Differentiation: Unlocking the Slopes of Complex Curves
target_audience: University Freshmen and Advanced High School Calculus Students

outline.topic: Implicit Differentiation: Unlocking the Slopes of Complex Curves
outline.target_audience: University Freshmen and Advanced High School Calculus Students

sections.title: The Great Divide: Explicit vs. Implicit
sections.content: Introduce the difference between explicit functions (y is isolated) and implicit equations (x and y are tangled). Use a visual of a 'solved' puzzle vs. a 'jumbled' puzzle. Explain that while we can't always solve for y, we can still find the rate of change.
sections.example: Explicit: y = x² (A simple path). Implicit: x² + y² = 25 (A circular racetrack where x and y are inseparable partners).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Reminder
sections.content: Review the Chain Rule as the 'Golden Key'. Emphasize that whenever we differentiate a term containing 'y' with respect to 'x', we must treat 'y' as an inner function [y(x)]. Graphically show a 'function within a function' as a set of nested Russian dolls.
sections.example: To differentiate y³, think of it as [f(x)]³. The derivative is 3y² multiplied by the 'hidden' derivative dy/dx.

sections.title: The Step-by-Step Algorithm
sections.content: Outline the three-step process: 1. Differentiate both sides with respect to x. 2. Apply the Chain Rule to all 'y' terms (tagging them with dy/dx). 3. Use algebra to isolate dy/dx on one side. Use an animation of a balance scale to show operations happening to both sides simultaneously.
sections.example: Visualizing 'dy/dx' as a specific colored 'sticky note' that gets attached to every term where y was differentiated.

sections.title: Guided Practice: The Circular Track
sections.content: Apply the steps to the equation of a circle x² + y² = 25. Show the transformation from an equation of position to an equation of slope. Use a character like 'Dash the Cheetah' running along the circle to represent a point (x, y).
sections.example: At point (3, 4) on the circle, we calculate dy/dx = -x/y. Plugging in the numbers, the cheetah's instantaneous direction (slope) is -3/4.

sections.title: Complex Curves: The Folium of Descartes
sections.content: Demonstrate the power of the technique on a 'looping' curve where solving for y is nearly impossible. Use a 3D-style animation to show how the tangent line 'glides' smoothly around the loop, even when the curve doubles back on itself.
sections.example: Equation: x³ + y³ = 6xy. Show how the Product Rule must be used on the right side (6x * y) to correctly find the slope of this 'looped' knot.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Insight
sections.content: Recap the core concept: Implicit differentiation allows us to find the slope (dy/dx) at any point on a curve without needing a clean 'y =' formula. End with a visual montage of various implicit shapes (ellipses, hyperbolas, and hearts) with their tangent lines flashing.
sections.example: A 'Heart Curve' (x² + y² - 1)³ - x²y³ = 0. Even for love, calculus can find the exact slope of the curve at any moment!

storyboard.title: The Great Divide: Explicit vs. Implicit
lecture_lines: In explicit functions, y is isolated and solved.
Implicit equations keep x and y tangled together.
We can still find slopes for complex curves.
animations: Display the equation 'y = x^2' in #FFFFFF at the top center. Label it 'Explicit' in #FFFF00.
Animate a puzzle piece with the label 'y' moving into a 'Solved' box.
Display the equation 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' in #00FF00 below the first. Label it 'Implicit' in #FF00FF.
Show 'x' and 'y' labels rotating around each other, signifying they are 'tangled'.
A dashed line (slope) appears next to the circle equation, representing the rate of change.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Reminder
lecture_lines: Think of y as a hidden inner function.
The chain rule is our essential golden key.
Differentiating y-cubed yields three y-squared times dy/dx.
animations: Display '[f(x)]^3' in #FFFFFF. Show the outer derivative 3[f(x)]^2 appearing in #00FFFF.
Highlight the inner function f(x) and show its derivative f'(x) being multiplied: 3[f(x)]^2 * f'(x).
Replace f(x) with 'y' and f'(x) with 'dy/dx' to show the final term: 3y^2 * (dy/dx) in #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: The Step-by-Step Algorithm
lecture_lines: First, differentiate both sides with respect to x.
Apply the chain rule to every y term.
Attach a dy/dx tag to those derivatives.
Group all dy/dx terms on one side.
Finally, isolate dy/dx to find the slope formula.
animations: Show a balance scale with 'd/dx' applied to both sides of the equation x^2 + y^2 = 25.
A bright pink 'sticky note' labeled 'dy/dx' attaches to the term where 'y' was differentiated.
Move all terms containing 'dy/dx' to the left side and isolate 'dy/dx' in a box.

storyboard.title: Guided Practice: The Circular Track
lecture_lines: Consider a circular track defined by this equation.
Differentiating gives two x plus two y dy/dx.
Notice how the constant twenty-five becomes zero.
At point three four, the slope is negative three-fourths.
The cheetah's direction changes as it orbits the center.
animations: Draw a circle representing x^2 + y^2 = 25 and label it in #FFFFFF.
Place a point at (3, 4) and bring in [Asset: Dash the Cheetah] at that location.
Show the differentiation steps: 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, highlighting the Chain Rule result in #FFFF00.
Isolate dy/dx to show the formula dy/dx = -x/y in #00FFFF.
Calculate the slope at (3, 4) as -3/4 and draw a tangent line at the cheetah's position.

storyboard.title: Complex Curves: The Folium of Descartes
lecture_lines: Some curves loop and cross over themselves.
Solving for y here is nearly impossible.
Use the product rule on the right side.
Calculus finds slopes even at the loop's crossing.
The tangent line glides smoothly along the curve.
animations: Plot the Folium of Descartes (x^3 + y^3 = 6xy) in #FF00FF.
Zoom into the curve's loop to show the complexity where x and y values overlap.
Apply the Product Rule to the term 6xy, showing 6y + 6x(dy/dx) in #FFFF00.
Show the algebraic steps to isolate dy/dx = (6y - 3x^2) / (3y^2 - 6x) in #FFFFFF.
Animate a tangent line gliding around the loop, showing its slope changing continuously.

storyboard.title: Summary and Geometric Insight
lecture_lines: Implicit differentiation unlocks slopes for any complex shape.
We find dy/dx without isolating y first.
From circles to hearts, calculus reveals every slope.
animations: Display a montage of implicit shapes like an ellipse, hyperbola, and a heart in different colors.
Flash tangent lines at various points on each shape to show the derivative's application.
Display the summary text: 'Implicit Differentiation: Any curve, any slope!' in #FFFF00.
